title: Chapter 7: RDS for SQL Server vs Azure SQL: When to Choose Which

questions.q: The chapter calls which mistake the most common in this evaluation?
options: Comparing prices without including storage
Treating 'Azure SQL' as one product instead of evaluating Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance separately
Forgetting about backup retention
Choosing based on the company’s existing cloud
questions.explain: The chapter warns that on Azure there are two very different products — SQL Database (PaaS, no Agent) and Managed Instance (near-full engine compatibility) — and treating 'Azure SQL' as one thing is the most common evaluation mistake.

questions.q: How does Azure Hybrid Benefit change the cost comparison?
options: It lets you apply existing SQL Server licenses with active Software Assurance to Azure SQL and pay only the compute rate — often 40%+ cheaper
It provides free storage for the first year
It only applies to development subscriptions
It converts License Included pricing to BYOL automatically
questions.explain: The chapter calls Azure Hybrid Benefit Azure's killer feature: with licenses plus active SA you pay only the compute rate, which can reduce the bill by 40% or more versus license-included pricing.

questions.q: An application inventory shows heavy SQL Server Agent jobs, linked servers, CLR assemblies, and cross-database queries. Per the chapter, this eliminates:
options: RDS for SQL Server
SQL Server on EC2
Azure SQL Managed Instance
Azure SQL Database — leaving RDS vs Managed Instance to be decided by licensing and estate gravity
questions.explain: The chapter's feature map shows SQL Database has no Agent, no linked servers, no CLR, and no cross-database joins — that inventory eliminates SQL Database, while RDS and MI support those features.

options: A VPN tunnel between on-premises and Azure
A read-only replica link for reporting
A near-zero-downtime migration path that replicates from on-premises SQL Server to Managed Instance over Always On technology
A licensing bridge for BYOL on Azure
questions.explain: The chapter describes the MI link as the smoothest SQL Server cloud migration path: online, built on AG replication, with rollback by failing back to the primary.

questions.q: What is the FIRST step in the chapter's decision framework?
options: Measure log generation rate on-premises
Check existing Microsoft licenses with Software Assurance — licensing decides before technology does
Run the Data Migration Assistant
Compare failover times across platforms
questions.explain: The framework applies in order and the first factor that fires usually decides: existing Microsoft licenses with SA, priced via Azure Hybrid Benefit versus RDS BYOL/LI, decides more evaluations than all technical criteria combined.
